title: There aren’t 100 good TV shows
gist: Yglesias disputes the premise of the New York Times '100 Best TV Shows of the 21st Century' list. He argues that because TV is a cost-controlled, grind-it-out business, prestige TV retreated quickly into the economic constraints that keep the medium mostly mediocre. Location choices, such as shooting D.C. stories in Canada, show how every creative choice is also a business decision.

insights.claim: Yglesias argues every creative choice in film and TV is also a business decision, especially in television, where many projects are produced and cost control matters a lot.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Content quality at studios and streamers is constrained by unit economics, not just talent.
insights.quote: Every creative choice in film or television is also a business decision — and that’s especially true in television.

insights.claim: With movies, the main business question is which projects get made at all, whereas television is a grind-it-out medium where cost control dominates.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Explains different margin structures in film and TV production.

insights.claim: Washington, D.C. is an expensive place to film, so productions like the first season of 'The Night Agent' shoot in Canada and pass it off as D.C.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Production cost arbitrage keeps flowing to Canadian locations, benefiting the Canadian production sector.
insights.quote: It’s common for projects like the first season of “The Night Agent” to shoot in Canada and just say it’s D.C.

insights.claim: Novels let writers work without budget limits but pay poorly, a tradeoff that shapes where creative talent goes.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Talent flows toward better-paid but budget-constrained screen work.

insights.claim: Yglesias contends that from the vantage point of 2026, 'The Sopranos' showed TV could host great ambitious storytelling, but the medium mostly has not delivered on that promise.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Skeptical view of the durability of 'prestige' content as a differentiator for streaming platforms.

insights.claim: The 'prestige' TV boom sparked by 'The Sopranos' retreated relatively quickly into the same tropes and economic constraints that have always made television mediocre.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Points to mean reversion in content spending ambition across the TV industry.
insights.quote: so-called “prestige” television retreated relatively quickly into the same tropes and economic constraints that have always made television a land of mediocrity.

insights.claim: Yglesias disputes the premise of the New York Times '100 Best TV Shows of the 21st Century' list, arguing there are not 100 good TV shows and that such lists mainly drive argument and engagement.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Shows how media outlets use list content as an engagement play.
insights.quote: I just kind of dispute the premise that there are 100 good TV shows.

insights.claim: Cultural commentary often takes creative output at face value and ignores the 'how the sausage gets made' economics, much as political journalism would if it ignored the legislative process.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: A lens for reading entertainment-industry coverage critically.
